e: From Ancient Greek κυκεών (kukeṓn), from κυκάω (kukáō, “I mix”).

q: New York is to me a scream — a kyke’s dream of a ghetto.
1922, T. Dreiser, “letter”, in archived in secondary sources:
He was a Kyke and this was his way to get back for all those Nazi concentration camps.
1959, G.P. Morrill, “Dark Sea Running”, in Green’s Dictionary of Slang:
drummers called the Russian Jew ... a Kyke.
